    🌍 Terrain Surfaces

    Hex Terrains Framework supports multiple surface types (like ground or water), each implemented as a HexSurfaceLayer. These surfaces are responsible for storing key data such as height, biomes, and render information. Surfaces are extensible, fully ECS-compatible, and processed with DOTS for maximum performance.

    Surface Types

    Each surface type is implemented as a class that inherits from HexSurfaceLayer. The primary concrete implementations include:

    • HexGroundLayer – for terrain ground surface (elevation, terrain biomes).
    • WaterSurfaceLayer (not shown here, but supported similarly).

    Each surface has associated systems to handle metric calculation and rendering-related preprocessing.

    🧱 Structure of a Surface Layer

    Each HexSurfaceLayer holds multiple data layers, such as:

    Data Layer Purpose
    HeightMap Stores per-cell elevation
    BiomesMap Stores biome index per cell
    CellColorMap Stores visualized colors for each cell
    CellMetrics Stores combined metrics derived from height + biome
    BiomeColors A palette for converting biome index to color

    All of these layers are implemented as DataLayer or ChunkedDataLayer objects and benefit from read/write dependency tracking and chunk-level dirty maps for efficient job scheduling.

    🧪 Data Generation and Setup

    Surfaces can be initialized via authoring components in the Unity Editor. For example:

    Example: HexGroundLayerAuthoring

    public class HexGroundLayerAuthoring : HexSurfaceLayerAuthoring {}

    When baked by HexGroundDataBaker, this authoring component:

    • Sets up height, biomes, and color palette.
    • Adds the HexGroundColorPalette buffer to the terrain entity.
    • Schedules a CreateHexGroundLayerRequest.
    public struct CreateHexGroundLayerRequest : ICreateHexSurfaceRequest, IComponentData

    This request is then picked up by systems to construct the ECS-side surface representation.

    ⚙️ Simulation and Updates

    Color Map Generation: CalcCellBiomeColorsSystem<T>

    This system:

    • Compares dirty flags between biomes and color maps.
    • Combines chunk-level dirty grids.
    • Schedules a CalculateBiomesColorMapJob or CalculateWaterColorMapJob.
    • Writes biome color to CellColorMap using the defined palette.

    The system ensures color maps update only when needed, and processes data in jobs chunk-by-chunk.

    Metrics Calculation: CalcCellMetricsSystem<T>

    Surface metrics such as slope, average height, or relative biome data are calculated here.

    • Depends on HeightMap and BiomesMap.
    • Uses ChunkDirtyGrid to identify regions needing recalculation.
    • Populates CellMetrics (metrics and cell position data).

    Specialized implementation:

    public partial class CalcGroundCellMetricsSystem : CalcCellMetricsSystem<HexGroundLayer>

    🔄 Runtime Behavior

    • Systems are designed to work independently per terrain, which allows multi-terrain setups.
    • Surfaces automatically react to changes in their layers (e.g., biome or heightmap changes) via their dirty flags and dependency tracking.

    🌈 Color Palette System

    For visual feedback (e.g., biomes displayed in the minimap or by coloring cells on terrain):

    • Each surface has a color palette (e.g., HexGroundColorPalette).
    • The palette is used during biome color map job execution.
    • Supports easy customization and visualization without needing shader-side logic.

    🧩 Custom Surfaces

    To create a custom surface:

    1. Derive from HexSurfaceLayer.
    2. Create an authoring component and baker.
    3. Implement a data creation request (ICreateHexSurfaceRequest).
    4. Add custom systems for metric or render preparation as needed.

    Here's a structured documentation section for the Terrain Surfaces system in your Hex Terrains Framework:

    Terrain Surfaces

    Hex Terrains Framework supports multiple surface types (e.g., ground, water) using a flexible and extensible layer system. Each surface is implemented as a specialized HexSurfaceLayer and may store height data, biome information, color maps, and associated rendering data. This section details how terrain surfaces are constructed, managed, raycasted, and updated.

    Overview

    A HexSurface is a conceptual layer of the terrain, such as the ground or water. Each one is implemented via:

    • A derived class from HexSurfaceLayer
    • A HeightMapDataLayer for cell heights (as byte, scaled to world meters)
    • A CellBiomesDataLayer for storing biome types per cell
    • A CellColorsDataLayer for coloring the surface, updated based on biomes or other logic
    • A HexTerrainRenderData layer to render the surface mesh

    Example surface layers:

    • HexGroundLayer (ground surface)
    • HexWaterLayer (custom surface type, if added)
    • Each implements ICreateHexSurfaceDataRequest or uses associated request structs for instantiation

    Layer Creation

    Surfaces are initialized by systems such as CreateHexGroundLayerRequest and CreateHexSurfaceRequestArgs, usually via authoring components like HexGroundLayerAuthoring or HexSurfaceLayerAuthoring. These components describe what kind of surface to create and associate them with a terrain entity.

    Example Setup Flow

    HexGroundLayerAuthoring -> CreateHexGroundLayerRequest
→ System receives request → Creates HexGroundLayer
→ Initializes DataLayers (HeightMap, Biomes, Colors)

    Cleanup

    Each surface is cleaned every frame (if visible) to clear dirty flags or release temporary resources.

    • Base class: CleanupHexSurfaceLayerSystem<TSurface>
    • Example implementation: CleanupHexGroundLayerSystem
    public class CleanupHexGroundLayerSystem 
    : CleanupHexSurfaceLayerSystem<HexGroundLayer>
{
    protected override void OnUpdate() { ... }
}

    The system checks HexTerrainVisibility.Value before calling surface.CleanupAsync().

    Surface Color Map Calculation

    The biomes map drives the visual appearance of terrain via CalculateBiomesColorMapJob. This job:

    • Iterates over each cell in parallel
    • Skips clean (non-dirty) chunks
    • Maps the biome index (byte) to a Color32 using a palette
    • Writes results into CellColorsDataLayer
    if (cellValue < Colors.Length)
    CellColorMap[index] = Colors[cellValue];
else
    CellColorMap[index] = DefaultColor;

    This allows efficient color map recalculation per chunk.

    Raycasting

    Two raycasting jobs exist for interaction and tooling:

    RaycastHexTerrainJob

    Raycasts against a single surface's heightmap. It:

    • Iterates along the ray by steps
    • Converts world coordinates to hex cell index
    • Checks if the point is under the surface's height

    If so, it writes a HexTerrainRaycastData containing:

    • IsHit
    • HitPosition
    • CellCoord, CellIndex, ChunkIndex, ChunkCoord

    RaycastHexTerrain2Job

    Works similarly, but checks two surfaces simultaneously (e.g., ground and water) and picks the one with higher height at each cell.

    var rawHeight = max(Heightmap1[cellIndex], Heightmap2[cellIndex]);

    This enables correct behavior for raycasts involving layered terrain.

    Terrain Metrics

    The CalcHexCellMetricsJob and CalcCellMetricsSystem compute per-cell properties like slope, height, and elevation, used for physics, rendering, or gameplay logic. These systems run after terrain data changes and update internal terrain state accordingly.

    Summary

    Hex Terrain Surfaces provide an efficient and extensible way to represent elevation, biomes, and visual data. Each surface is ECS-native and fully integrated into the simulation loop, using chunked data layers, dirty tracking, and job scheduling for high performance. Whether you're rendering a mountain range or simulating ocean waves, HexSurfaceLayer is the foundation that supports terrain realism in the framework.
